title: Aretha Franklin's birth chart
metaDescription: Aretha Franklin's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 4.4° Aries. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Sun stands at 4.4° Aries, in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Measured rather than labelled, the Sun holds 4.4° Aries: the first decan, whose classical sub-ruler is Mars. A fire sign, read here in its first face.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Closer in, Mercury stands at 12.4° Pisces; Venus stands at 19.8° Aquarius; Mars stands at 10.9° Gemini. The tradition reads a mind that absorbs before it argues from Mercury, taste led by wit and proportion from Venus, drive that argues its way forward from Mars.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Start where the chart is tightest — the Sun trine Pluto, 0.8° of separation. A trine runs downhill — the talent that never announces itself because it never had to. Behind it, Uranus trine Neptune at 0.9°, and Mercury square Mars at 1.5° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The day-stable angles form no closed figure. Nothing funnels; each aspect is its own negotiation, which the tradition reads as a chart of separate treaties rather than one campaign.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Four planets here sit in a sign the classical scheme scores. The Sun in Aries at 4.4° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; the Moon in Cancer at 12.2° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Mercury in Pisces at 12.4° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Jupiter in Gemini at 15.0° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The honest balance sheet uses the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: air 3, earth 3, fire 2, water 2 across the elements, and mutable 4, fixed 4, cardinal 2 across the modalities. An air-weighted chart thinks in through-lines; the sentence is how it takes hold of the world. Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — motion that reverses only from this vantage point, and which the old reading treats as delay used for revision.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Cancer for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.0° between midnight and midnight. Fast enough that its degree is approximate, slow enough that its sign is not in doubt. At the noon reference it stands at 12.2°.
